verses.1: I do not want to hide from you, brothers, that all our ancestors were also affected by the sky, and they all traveled through the sea.
verses.2: And all of them were baptized in the sky and in the sea, according to Moses’ command.
verses.3: And they all consumed that spiritual substance.
verses.4: And all that spiritual gift was also a spiritual thing. It came from a spiritual source. And that source was Christ himself.
verses.5: But God did not approve of them being among the majority. They were destroyed in the wilderness.
verses.6: These are the ways in which our kind have become like this, so that we will not be willing to do evil, just as those others were also unwilling to do it.
verses.7: And do not become idolaters, like some of them. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and they began to play games.”
verses.8: And we were not also sold as slaves, since some of them were already sold and died within a day. There were twenty-three thousand people who died in that day.
verses.9: Nor do we try Christ, for some of them tried him, and they were rejected by those who were deceived.
verses.10: Do not be deceived, as some of them have been deceived. They lost everything because of this deception.
verses.11: These things happened in their own way. They wrote them down for our sake, so that we would remember them when the days of eternity come.
verses.12: So that I can see that he doesn’t fall.
verses.13: The trial you are going through is not meant to be a test of human strength. But God, who is faithful, will not let you be tested beyond your limits. Instead, through this trial, He will show you how much you truly can do.
verses.14: Therefore, my beloved, abandon the worship of idols.
verses.15: I say as if it were a matter of thoughtfulness; you yourselves decide what I mean.
verses.16: The cup of blessing that we offer is not a sharing in the blood of Christ. The bread that we eat is not a sharing in the body of Christ.
verses.17: Because one loaf of bread constitutes one body for many people. After all, we all come from that single loaf of bread.
verses.18: Look at Israel in its physical form. Aren’t those who offer sacrifices also part of the altar?
verses.19: So what do I mean? That I know what an idol is, or that I understand what an idol is.
verses.20: But what they offer as sacrifices are things that belong to demons, not to God. I do not want you to become companions of demons.
verses.21: You shall not use cups for the Lord’s wine, nor for the demons’ wine. You shall not use a table for the Lord, nor a table for the demons.
verses.22: Or shall we call him “the Lord”? Are we not stronger than him?
verses.23: It’s always okay; but not always suitable. It’s always okay; but not everyone will be happy with it.
verses.24: No one should seek what is for themselves, but what is for others.
verses.25: Everything that is sold in the market should be consumed without any investigation, out of mere indifference.
verses.26: For the lord’s land is also its wealth.
verses.27: If anyone calls you “fools” and wants to lead you astray, then accept everything that is given to you without questioning it, out of sheer awareness.
verses.28: If anyone says to you, “This is a sacred place; do not touch the things that belong here, nor do you eat from it.”
verses.29: I say that consciousness is not about oneself, but about others. For how can my freedom be judged by another’s consciousness?
verses.30: If I am involved in this, then why should I be ashamed of it?
verses.31: Whether you eat, drink, or do anything else, do it all in the sight of God.
verses.32: May you become obedient to God’s Church, both to the Jews and to the Greeks.
verses.33: Since I like everyone everywhere, I don’t consider my own interests first; instead, I think about what’s best for many people, so that they can be saved.
